extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners handling filings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting requirements for receipt, handling, and filing-date entitlement of U.S. patent applications (nonprovisional, provisional, continued prosecution, design, and international). Covers postcard receipts, filing receipts, confirmation numbers, fee/payment and oath requirements, completeness standards, and subsequent treatment of filed papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary application number on return postcard is not controlling
rubrics_metrics.description: The application number identified on a postcard receipt is merely the preliminary assignment of an application number to the application, and should not be relied upon (e.g., with respect to foreign filings) as necessarily representing the application number assigned to such application. See 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing receipt mailed by OIPE (see below) represents the official assignment of an application number; as between inconsistent filing receipts and postcard receipts, the application number on the filing receipt is controlling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identifying data on return postcard
rubrics_metrics.description: The identifying data on the postcard should include: (A) applicant’s name(s); (B) title of invention; (C) number of pages of specification, claims (for nonprovisional applications), and sheets of drawing; (D) whether oath or declaration is included; (E) a list of any additional forms included with the application (e.g., application transmittal form, application data sheet, fee transmittal form, and/or provisional application cover sheet); and (F) amount and manner of paying the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A return postcard should be attached to each patent application for which a receipt is desired. It is important that the return postcard itemize all of the components of the application; otherwise it will not serve as evidence that any component which was not itemized was received by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return postcard must itemize each component to serve as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The postcard receipt will not serve as prima facie evidence of receipt of any item which is not adequately itemized on the postcard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely listing 'a complete application' or 'patent application' is not sufficient. Each separate component (specification including written description, claims and abstract; number of claims; sheets of drawings; pages of oath/declaration; pages of cover sheet for provisional) should be specifically and properly itemized on the postcard. Incorporation by reference to a transmittal letter will not serve as prima facie evidence of receipt of those items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postcard postage and meter-postmark rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure the receipt of return receipt postcards, users must either: (A) purchase already stamped postcards from USPS or affix postage stamps to their postcards; or (B) if a postage meter is used, ensure that the meter postmark does not show the date. Any return receipt postcard containing a dated meter postmark may not be delivered by USPS to the address provided on the postcard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are solely responsible for placing proper postage on self-addressed postcards. Check with USPS regarding postage and acceptable card sizes. Any postcard lacking sufficient postage or not acceptable may not be delivered and, if returned to the USPTO, may be discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing receipt contents and controlling effect
rubrics_metrics.description: OIPE mails a filing receipt to the attorney/agent or applicant for each application filed which meets the minimum requirements to receive a filing date. The filing receipt includes the application number, filing date, a confirmation number, a suggested class in the U.S. Patent Classification System, and the number of an art unit where the application is likely to be examined. The filing receipt represents the official assignment by the USPTO of a specific application number and confirmation number to a particular application. See 37 CFR 1.54(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application number officially assigned on the filing receipt may differ from the number on a postcard receipt; where inconsistent, the application number on the filing receipt controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation number assignment and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The confirmation number is a four-digit number assigned to each newly filed application. In combination with the application number it is used to verify the accuracy of the application number placed on correspondence to avoid misidentification due to transposition errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The confirmation number is found on the filing receipt and on PAIR. It must be used when submitting an EFS copy of the application for publication to verify correct identification. The Office recommends applicants include the confirmation number (in addition to the application number) on all correspondence concerning the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney docket number format limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney docket numbers must be limited to a maximum of 12 characters to prevent truncation. The PALM database allows a maximum of 12 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spaces, slashes, and hyphens will no longer be included in the entered docket number on the official filing receipt. If CASE or NAVY-CASE appears before the first character, only the characters after CASE or NAVY-CASE will be entered on the official filing receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filed applications that meet minimum requirements will not be returned
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications which are entitled to a filing date and are filed, whether by regular mail, Express Mail under 37 CFR 1.10, hand-delivery, the Office’s Electronic Filing System (EFS), or otherwise, will not be returned to applicant even if requested. See 37 CFR 1.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be careful not to file applications not intended to be filed (e.g., duplicates). A change of purpose after payment of a fee does not entitle the party to a refund (37 CFR 1.26(a)); see MPEP § 607.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postcard receipt verification procedure at USPTO intake
rubrics_metrics.description: The person receiving the item(s) in the USPTO will check the listing on the postcard against the items being filed to ensure they are properly identified and that all listed items are presently being submitted. Items not submitted will be crossed off and the postcard initialed by the person receiving the items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon return, the postcard should be promptly reviewed by the filer to ensure every item denoted was received. If annotated to indicate an item was not received, that item will not have prima facie evidence of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Date stamp rules and what constitutes 'filing date'
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO stamps papers and fees with the date of their receipt in the Office (the 'Office Date' stamp). When the last day for taking action or paying a fee falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within D.C., the action or fee is considered timely if taken or paid on the next succeeding business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence filed under 37 CFR 1.10 will be stamped with the date of deposit as 'Express Mail'. Facsimile transmissions are stamped with the date the complete transmission is received unless that date is a weekend/holiday, in which case the next business day is stamped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of provisional pendency when 12-month anniversary falls on weekend/holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Law 106-113 amended 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3) to extend the period of pendency of a provisional application to the next succeeding business day if the day that is 12 months after the filing date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within D.C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to provisional applications filed on or after June 8, 1995; see 37 CFR 1.7(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional application filing-date entitlement (37 CFR 1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a nonprovisional application is the date on which a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 containing a description pursuant to § 1.71 and at least one claim pursuant to § 1.75, and any drawing required by § 1.81(a) are filed in the Office. No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuing application (continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part) may be filed under specified statutory conditions. If the purported specification is so informal and incoherent that it clearly does not constitute a specification under 35 U.S.C.112 and 37 CFR1.71, the application will not be accorded a filing date until corrections are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application filing-date entitlement and cover-sheet requirement (37 CFR 1.53(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application is the date on which a specification as prescribed by the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C.112, and any drawing required by § 1.81(a) are filed. A cover sheet (37 CFR1.51(c)(1)), which may be an application data sheet (§1.76) or a cover letter identifying the application as provisional, is required to prevent it from being treated as a nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment other than to make the provisional comply with statute/regulations may be made after filing. Requirements regarding nucleotide/amino acid sequence disclosures (§§1.821-1.825) are not mandatory for provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of nonprovisional to provisional, and provisional to nonprovisional
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under paragraph (b) may be converted to a provisional application and accorded the original filing date if accompanied by the processing fee and filed prior to certain events. A provisional may be converted to a nonprovisional and accorded the provisional filing date if conversion is accompanied by required fees and an amendment including at least one claim (unless provisional already contains a claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion does not entitle applicant to refund of fees or application of previously paid fees to the new filing; conversion to nonprovisional may result in patent term being measured from at least the provisional filing date (adverse to applicant). Applicants should consider filing a nonprovisional claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C.119(e) instead of converting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) rules (37 CFR 1.53(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A continued prosecution application (CPA) filed under 37 CFR1.53(d) (design applications only) will be assigned the application number of the prior application for identification purposes. A CPA must identify the prior application, disclose and claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior application, name as inventors the same inventors named in the prior application (subject to limited exceptions), and be filed before specified events (e.g., payment of issue fee, abandonment, termination of proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing fee, search fee, and examination fee for a CPA are set by §1.16. A CPA may utilize the file jacket and contents of the prior application; no amendment in a CPA may introduce new matter. Filing a CPA constitutes a waiver of confidentiality under 35 U.S.C.122 to the extent members of the public entitled to access to one application may be given similar access to related applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and procedure when filing-date requirements are not met
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application deposited under paragraphs (b), (c), or (d) does not meet the requirements to be entitled to a filing date, applicant will be notified (if correspondence address provided) and given a period to correct the filing error. Failure to correct within given time or timely petition may result in proceedings being terminated and application disposed of; fees (less handling fee) may be refunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for review of such notification must be by petition accompanied by the fee specified in §1.17(f). If a request for an application under paragraph (d) does not meet requirements because the underlying application is not a design application, and if that application was filed on or after June 8, 1995, the request will be treated as a request for continued examination under §1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of application subsequent to filing—payment of fees and oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application accorded a filing date does not include the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, or an oath/declaration, and applicant has provided a correspondence address, applicant will be notified and given time to pay the fees and file the oath/declaration and any surcharge to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no correspondence address was provided, applicant has two months from filing date to submit missing fees and oath/declaration. Excess claims fees and multiple dependent claim fees not paid on filing must be paid or claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the Office-set reply period. Failure to pay basic filing fee during pendency may result in Office disposing of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent treatment of applications lacking required parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application filed under paragraphs (b) or (d) will not be placed on the files for examination until all its required parts, complying with the rules, are received, except that certain minor informalities may be waived subject to subsequent correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional application will not be placed on the files for examination and will become abandoned no later than twelve months after its filing date pursuant to 35 U.S.C.111(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete nonprovisional application grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: If nonprovisional application papers filed under 37 CFR1.53(b) do not include at least a specification containing a description and at least one claim and a drawing if necessary under 35 U.S.C.113, or if the papers are too informal to be given a filing date, the case is held as an incomplete application and no filing date is granted until incompleteness is corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice of Incomplete Application is mailed when nonprovisional application papers are deemed incomplete. Components necessary to obtain a filing date are: specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C.112 and 37 CFR1.71; a claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C.112 and 37 CFR1.75; and a drawing if required by 35 U.S.C.113 and 37 CFR1.81(a). Even if components purport to be present, they must satisfy statutory and regulatory requirements; obviously informal/incoherent documents will be unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date of an international application designating the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an international application designating the United States of America is treated as the filing date in the United States under PCT Article 11(3), except as provided in 35 U.S.C.102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See relevant statutes and PCT provisions for exceptions.
